title: Playing with Gerry Mulligan
summary: Mulligan sat in everywhere; they performed together for decades, including a 1990s European tour.

blocks.x: Let me ask you about Gerry Mulligan and then we will take a break. Tell me about that collaboration. How did you approach that? Would you approach playing with Gerry the same way you would with Paul? How did that come about? There was a lengthy period there where you often collaborated with Gerry.
Yeah, and Paul often played with Gerry.

He was a musician that couldn’t resist playing when he was around. He just had to sit in, and nobody would say, “Don’t sit in” to him, because it always seemed to add something that just propelled whatever group he sat in with. I remember at the Newport Jazz Festival George Wein saying, “That Gerry. He’s all over the place, sitting in with everybody.” Maybe some people didn’t like it, but I liked it. We first got to know each other in that period where I brought him to Fantasy. Then we often did concerts where his group would play and then my group, or my group and then
his group, depending on the situation. [ ] in Europe with both groups. Russell, would you remember the years?
We toured together all over Europe. He had a very strong group.
They both married Mills [College] girls. You remember?
